levels.title: Testing pico applications
levels.description: Fast, isolated tests for pico apps with the pico-testing pytest plugin.

levels.title: Why isolation is the default
levels.description:
The shared-venv trap

Every pico plugin installed in your environment is auto-discovered by pico_boot.init(). That is great in production and terrible in tests: a suite that passes on your machine can fail on a colleague's just because they have one more pico package installed - or worse, pass for the wrong reason.

The pico-testing plugin closes that hole by default. Installing it activates a pytest plugin (no conftest wiring) that sets PICO_BOOT_AUTO_PLUGINS=false for every test, so a container only ever contains what the test asked for.

It also ships two fixtures:

  • make_container(*modules, config=None, boot=False) - builds containers and shuts them all down on teardown, newest first.
  • make_client(container) - a FastAPI TestClient with the lifespan running (needs a local terminal: the browser runtime has no threads).

levels.title: Containers from a fixture
levels.description:
make_container

The make_container fixture builds a container from explicit modules and config, and guarantees shutdown on teardown - no try/finally in your tests, no leaked containers between tests.

A plain dict passed as config is wrapped in configuration(DictSource(...)) for you. Complete the second test: build the container with a config that flips the greeting style to loud.

files.name: app.py
test_main.py
files.content:
import app

def test_greets_plainly_by_default(make_container):
    container = make_container(app)
    assert container.get(app.Greeter).greet("pico") == "Hello, pico."

def test_greets_loudly_with_config(make_container):
    # 👈 pass config={"greeting": {"style": "loud"}} to make_container
    container = make_container(app)
    assert container.get(app.Greeter).greet("pico") == "HELLO, PICO!"

solution.test_main.py:
import app

def test_greets_plainly_by_default(make_container):
    container = make_container(app)
    assert container.get(app.Greeter).greet("pico") == "Hello, pico."

def test_greets_loudly_with_config(make_container):
    container = make_container(app, config={"greeting": {"style": "loud"}})
    assert container.get(app.Greeter).greet("pico") == "HELLO, PICO!"

hints: make_container accepts config= as a plain dict; the prefix is the settings prefix.

levels.title: Declare the module under test once
levels.description:
The pico_module ini option

Almost every test in a project boots the same package. Since pico-testing 0.2.0 you declare it once under [tool.pytest.ini_options] and make_container() prepends it to every call: make_container() boots the package alone, make_container(extra) boots both.

Set pico_module = "app" in pyproject.toml so the test passes without naming the module.

files.name: app.py
test_main.py

hints: The value is the importable module name, exactly as you would pass it to init(modules=[...]).

levels.title: Opting back into auto-discovery
levels.description:
The pico_auto_plugins marker

Isolation is enforced through the PICO_BOOT_AUTO_PLUGINS environment variable: the plugin sets it to false for every test. A test that genuinely verifies entry-point discovery - and only that kind of test - opts back in with @pytest.mark.pico_auto_plugins.

Mark the second test so both pass.

files.name: test_main.py
files.content:
import os
import pytest

def test_isolated_by_default():
    assert os.environ["PICO_BOOT_AUTO_PLUGINS"] == "false"

# 👈 add @pytest.mark.pico_auto_plugins
def test_discovery_allowed_when_marked():
    assert "PICO_BOOT_AUTO_PLUGINS" not in os.environ

hints: The marker is registered by the plugin itself; no import beyond pytest is needed.

levels.title: HTTP tests and teardown guarantees
levels.description:
make_client

With pico-fastapi installed, make_client(container) wraps the container's app in a TestClient with the lifespan actually running - so request-scoped controllers, startup hooks and shutdown wiring behave exactly as under uvicorn:

def test_endpoint(make_container, make_client):
    container = make_container("pico_fastapi", config={"fastapi": {"title": "t"}})
    client = make_client(container)
    assert client.get("/ping").status_code == 200

Closing the client fires the pico-fastapi lifespan shutdown AND the fixture shuts the container down again - a double shutdown that is safe because PicoContainer.shutdown() is idempotent since pico-ioc 2.3.3. This exact sequence was the root cause of a real teardown hang; the fixture bakes the correct pattern in.

TestClient uses threads, so this fixture needs a real terminal - it does not run in this browser environment. See the pico-examples repository for complete suites using it.
